title: Thunderstorms
description: Why warm air rises and storms form

lessons.title: What is a thunderstorm?
lessons.body: A thunderstorm is a storm that produces lightning and thunder. It needs warm, moist air.
lessons.key_idea: Warm, moist air rises and helps create thunderstorms.

lessons.title: Why does warm air rise?
lessons.body: Warm air is less dense than cooler air, so it rises through surrounding cooler, denser air.

lessons.title: The role of moisture
lessons.body: Moisture provides the water that forms clouds and rain inside the storm.

quiz.text: Why does warm air rise during thunderstorm formation?
options: Because warm air is less dense
Because warm air contains no moisture
quiz.why: Warm air is less dense, so it rises through cooler, denser air. This rising warm, moist air helps thunderstorms develop.
quiz.misconception: Clouds don't push warm air upward — warm air rises because it is less dense.

quiz.text: What happens when warm, less-dense air meets cooler, denser air?
options: It sinks below the cooler air
It rises above the cooler air
quiz.why: Less-dense warm air tends to rise above cooler, denser air.
quiz.misconception: It doesn't sink — warm air rises.

quiz.text: Which is most needed for a thunderstorm?
quiz.why: Warm, moist air provides energy and moisture for storm clouds.
Charge separation inside storm clouds creates lightning.
quiz.misconception: Lightning is not from clouds pushing.

quiz.why: Warm air → less dense → rises is the core idea.

lessons.title: What is humidity?
lessons.body: Humidity tells how much water vapor is in the air.

lessons.title: Why does humidity feel uncomfortable?
lessons.body: When humidity is high, sweat evaporates more slowly. So 32°C humid feels hotter than 32°C dry.
lessons.key_idea: Sweat cools you less when humid.

quiz.text: Why does high humidity make the same temperature feel hotter?
quiz.why: High humidity slows sweat evaporation, so your body cools less.
quiz.misconception: It's not thinner air — it's slower evaporation.

lessons.title: How rain forms
lessons.body: Water vapor cools, condenses into droplets, and falls when heavy enough.

quiz.why: Droplets grow and fall when heavy enough.

title: Heat Wave
description: What happens, why it occurs, safety

lessons.title: What is a heat wave?
lessons.body: Prolonged period of unusually hot weather, often with high humidity.
